title: Minimax Rates for Two-Visit Threshold-Clamp Modified Treatment Policy Effects
banked_reason: D0.5 cold referee graded the sound fixed-positive two-atom frontier subfield below the field floor; paper score ceiling 7.2 is below 7.4 and the scope is not salvageable.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

The boundary theorem proves only a necessary derivative component and refutes the proposed three-component frontier; it supplies neither a corrected achievable rate nor a matched boundary characterization.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a fixed-positive two-atom matched MSE and honest connected-interval frontier, plus a necessary obstruction for shrinking thresholds. The D0.5 cold referee graded that scoped result subfield, below the field novelty floor, and found no bounded field-level rescue; the shrinking-threshold frontier remains open. A subsequent independent math audit cleared all five initial panel findings for downgraded banking. No F-stage Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: The fixed-positive two-visit flat max-clamp slope has matched minimax MSE \(n^{-2\beta/(2\beta+2)}\) and honest connected-interval expected length \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+2)}\), uniformly over the threshold rectangle and over all measurable, possibly randomized procedures. The observable upper construction combines a history-indexed orthogonal second-stage pseudo-outcome with stabilized first-atom local polynomials, and a coupled same-class two-treatment bump supplies the converse. Each lower alternative now has an explicit independent-exogenous-variable causal lift satisfying strong sequential randomization, consistency, and all three structural-version conditions. By elementary monotonicity, the converse applies to a larger observed or causal model only after that model is proved to contain these witnesses; no larger-class upper bound is claimed. The separate shrinking-threshold frontier remains open, subject to the already-proved transported-face obstruction.
gap: Published longitudinal modified-policy theory gives efficient-influence-function inference for shift policies, including a threshold-triggered shift example, but it does not deliver the matched MSE and honest connected-length frontier for a fixed positive pair of flat max-clamp atoms. Published continuous-dose orthogonal learners likewise do not analyze the transported two-atom slope with an unknown continuous intermediate history.
fill: A completely specified cross-fitted orthogonal second-stage correction, ordinary joint Hölder nuisance estimability, stable first-atom transport, unconditional finite-sample risk and coverage accounting, and a legal coupled corner experiment yield the matched fixed-positive minimax MSE and honest connected-interval length theorem. Strict containment establishes why the continuous-biomarker pseudo-outcome is needed outside the ancillary binary-intermediate subclass.
